items.text: pinball_loss(y, q_pred, levels); WQL (weighted quantile loss, normalised by Σ|y|), our CRPS approximation; document the approximation in ADR 0002-metrics.md.
MASE (seasonal period from config; fall back to lag-1 when no seasonality).
Coverage of the 80% (0.1–0.9) and 98% (0.01–0.99) intervals; mean interval width (scaled).
Fidelity metrics for later phases: student-vs-teacher quantile loss, median MAE vs teacher median.
Aggregation: per series → per suite with geometric mean of relative scores vs seasonal naive (as in GIFT-Eval) + arithmetic mean; bootstrap 95% CIs over series.
Tests: hand-computed examples; a check that WQL ≈ CRPS for a Gaussian with many quantiles (compare with the closed-form Gaussian CRPS).
Sine · two seasonalities (daily+weekly-like) · trend + seasonality · multiplicative seasonality (growing amplitude) · damped trend · exponential growth · logistic saturation
Level shift (step) · trend break · spikes/outliers in context · heteroscedastic noise · missing-value gaps
Random walk · mean-reverting AR(1) · intermittent demand (mostly zeros) · sawtooth · square wave · chirp (rising frequency) · impulse + exponential decay · constant + noise
Tests: determinism per seed, shapes and dtypes, no NaN in future, meta records period and generating params.
A quick visual check: scripts/plot_shapes.py → results/figures/shapes_grid.png.
Baselines: seasonal naive (with empirical residual quantiles), ETS via statsforecast (with its intervals → quantiles).
Toto 2.0: the official small checkpoints (4m, 22m) + one larger checkpoint as teacher (pick the largest that keeps caching within budget; measure in 1.5).
t0: t0-gamma (the current release) if accessible, otherwise t0-alpha/beta; HF gated access via HF_TOKEN.
Chronos-2 (comparator).
Timestral 5M/28M/209M (comparator; owner confirmed licence eligibility 2026-11-13) (comparator only; see licence rule).
Contract test (tests/test_forecaster_contract.py, slow): every adapter returns (B, 13, H), monotone in the quantile axis, finite, and handles NaNs in the context.
make bench S=shapes runs all models configured in configs/eval/shapes.yaml and writes results/shapes/<model>.json (per-series metrics + forecasts as float16 for the gallery).
Latency: CPU, torch.set_num_threads(1) and 8, batch 1 and 32, warm-up then 50 timed runs → p50/p95. Record the hardware in the JSON. Also record param count and checkpoint size on disk.
scripts/build_web_data.py --suite shapes → web/public/data/gallery.json (shapes × models: context, quantiles, truth, WQL, MASE, latency).

Teacher throughput (CPU + Apple MPS; Kaggle T4 not measured) (windows/second) on CPU and on a Kaggle T4, at context 512 / horizon 64 → docs/notes/compute.md, plus a caching budget estimate for Phase 2.

Save the gallery figure (shapes × models small multiples), a summary table (relative WQL, latency, params), and the surprises (e.g. failure modes on multiplicative seasonality / intermittent series / level shifts) to the journal and results/figures/.

items.text: RTE éCO2mix (French national + regional electricity consumption, ~15/30 min): download script, resample to hourly (configurable), handle DST and gaps. Record the licence.
Open-Meteo historical weather (temperature for the same regions) — store now for optional Phase 8 covariates.
Optional extra real training data from open HF time-series corpora (e.g. Chronos / GIFT-Eval pretraining datasets). Document each licence; keep the total small.
Synthetic training corpus (synthetic.py): KernelSynth-style random GP kernel compositions + randomised versions of the shape generators + TSMixup-style mixing. Deterministic from seeds.
Define train_end, val_end, and the fresh test window (data strictly after the latest teacher release date used; record the dates and their sources in ADR 0003-splits.md).
tests/test_leakage.py: no training/validation window has a future timestamp ≥ val_end, no test window overlaps train, and gallery shapes use seeds disjoint from training seeds.
Secondary suite: a small GIFT-Eval subset, flagged "possibly seen by teachers".
Sample (context=512, horizon=64) windows with configurable stride, a minimum observed fraction, and NaN masks. Window ids are stable hashes (source, series_id, start index) so caches can be joined.
Sharded parquet: window_id, teacher, quantiles float16 (13, 64); optional samples for Toto (e.g. 64 samples float16) on a subset, used by the sample-pinball loss in Phase 4.
Resumable (skip completed shards), integrity check (counts, NaN check, monotonicity), and a manifest with teacher version + config hash.
Size the corpus from the 1.5 measurements: start with ~300k windows per teacher, then scale if the budget allows. Post the estimate, wait for approval, then run on Kaggle.
Also benchmark all models (teachers, Toto small checkpoints, baselines) on the fresh test split → results/fresh_fr_power/.

items.text: tinycast/models/student/: scaler (robust instance norm + optional asinh), patch embedding with NaN mask channel, a small transformer encoder, a quantile head with monotone construction. Also an MLP-only variant (N-HiTS-like) as an architecture ablation.
Size presets s/m/l (≈0.3M/1M/3M); print the param count at startup.

tinycast/distill/train.py: plain PyTorch loop: AdamW, cosine schedule with warm-up, grad clipping, AMP on GPU, gradient accumulation, early stopping on validation WQL, best-checkpoint saving, W&B + metrics.json logging.
Loss: pinball vs ground truth (L_gt).
Overfit test: the student overfits 64 windows to ~0 loss (catches bugs cheaply; make it a slow test).
Train s/m/l on ground truth only (same windows as the cache) → "GT-only floor", 3 seeds for m.
Short ADR 0004-student-architecture.md.
L_kd_quantile: per-level regression of student quantiles onto teacher quantiles, in scaled space (Huber), to test the "match the teacher's quantiles" view.
L_kd_pinball_teacher (also replaces the sample-pinball loss: Toto 2.0 has no samples): pinball of the student against the teacher's quantile values treated as pseudo-observations, weighted per level.

L_kd_sample_pinball — superseded: Toto 2.0 emits no samples; equivalent = mass-weighted L_kd_pinball_teacher (Toto samples): expected pinball under teacher samples. Its minimiser is exactly the teacher's quantile, a principled distribution-matching loss. Explain why in the journal; good article material.
Horizon weighting w(h) (uniform / linear increasing / learned), after DistilTS's observation that short horizons dominate the loss.
Mixed objective L = (1-α)·L_gt + α·L_kd.
E1: teacher ∈ {Toto, t0} × α ∈ {0, 0.5, 0.9, 1.0} for student m.

items.text: weighting.py: per-window teacher weights from each teacher's error on that window's ground truth (softmax(−τ·WQL)), with τ tuned on validation; compare to a uniform average and to the best single teacher. Optional: a tiny learned gating network on context features.
